entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, Section III.2, Paragraph 32 (Safety and Security)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and Their Protection', 21 May 2013
entries.provision: Article 7, Paragraph 4 (accuracy and reliability of personal data)
entries.why_here: Blocks out-of-range inputs (such as GPA 9.9 or negative exam scores tested in Part 4) before LLM inference so malformed records cannot produce arbitrary shortlist decisions.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, Section III.2, Paragraph 28 (Fairness and Non-Discrimination)
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan, 30 August 1995
entries.provision: Article 14, Paragraph 2 (prohibition of discrimination on grounds of origin, social status, gender, language, or other circumstances)
entries.why_here: Removes 'name' and 'university' before model inference to eliminate the statistically significant +2.5 point flagship-over-regional university score bias (sign p=0.002) and name-flip noise measured in Part 1.

entries.principle_source: OECD AI Principles (Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence), 2019 (amended 2024), Section 1, Principle 1.2 (Human-centred values and fairness)
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 94-V 'On Personal Data and Their Protection', 21 May 2013
entries.provision: Article 7, Paragraph 1 and Article 8 (purpose limitation and mandatory subject consent for personal data processing)
entries.why_here: Deterministically refuses unauthorized purposes (e.g., ethnicity ranking), minors (<18), missing consent, and prompt-injection strings in free-text fields with 0 model calls and 0/400 false refusals.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, Section III.2, Paragraph 37 (Transparency and Explainability)
entries.provision: Article 12, Paragraph 1 (automatic recording of events / logging for high-risk AI systems, applied here as an international governance benchmark)
entries.why_here: Writes one structured JSONL record per decision (storing hashes and field names rather than PII values) so every automated shortlist, reject, escalation, and refusal can be audited a year later.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence, 2021, Section III.2, Paragraph 35 (Human Oversight and Determination)
entries.provision: Article 14, Paragraph 1 and Annex III, Point 3(a) (human oversight for high-risk AI systems used in educational/scholarship access, applied as an international benchmark)
entries.why_here: Routes borderline scores in the (40, 49) overlap zone (where Part 1 showed 33 rejects and 31 shortlists) and merit-contradictory decisions to a human reviewer, escalating 9.0% (36/400) of applications.
